_schema_notes.purpose: Reference dataset of access-control (authentication/authorization) call-site shapes for JavaScript/TypeScript source, the AC-finder counterpart to llm_api_functions_js.json. Used by find_ac_points_js to scan frontend/backend JS/TS code for auth middleware, guards, decorators, and permission checks that RUPTA can never see (and that a Rust-only scan of a mixed Tauri-style app would miss entirely).
_schema_notes.usage: find_ac_points_js walks a directory of .js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs files. For each entry, it looks for the literal text `<pattern>(` on a line. If any of the entry's `packages` was also seen imported (via import/require/dynamic import) in the same file, match_strategy is "call+import"; otherwise "call-only". Both are reported for require_import:false entries; require_import:true entries are only reported when the import is confirmed.
_schema_notes.verification_caveat: These signatures come from general knowledge of each package's public API shape and have not been independently re-verified against current published docs. Spot-check against the target's actual installed version (package.json) before trusting a call-only match strongly.
_schema_notes.raw_http_note: The raw-http-authz entry has no call patterns of its own; find_ac_points_js treats any fetch()/axios()/http(s).request() call as a candidate and only reports it when a known access-control REST path suffix (shared AC_PATH_HINTS table in ac_hints.rs) is found in a string literal on a nearby line — mirrors raw-http-fetch in llm_api_functions_js.json. See --all-http-calls in find_ac_points_js to report every such call regardless of a path hint.
_schema_notes.generic_checks_note: generic-authz-checks has no associated npm package (it catches hand-rolled, in-house auth helpers like requireAuth()/hasRole()), so it can never be import-confirmed — every match is reported as call-only. This is intentionally noisier than the SDK-backed entries; read raw_line to judge relevance, and expect some hits on unrelated code that happens to share a common function name.
